title: Māṇḍūkyakārikā — Complete Four-Chapter Reader
subtitle: Gauḍapāda’s four-part commentary on the Māṇḍūkya Upaniṣad

source.edition: Māṇḍūkya Upaniṣad and Gauḍapāda-kārikā, A.K. Aruna format, 2022 version 6.0.

source.sanskrit: Devanāgarī text from Śāradā Peetham, Sringeri, as credited by the source edition.

source.changes: Arranged as a local reader of only the 215 numbered Kārikā verses. Upaniṣad mantras, Śaṅkara Bhāṣya, and Ṭīkā glosses are excluded. English translations spanning multiple Sanskrit verses are displayed with range labels. Editorial introductions before some verses are omitted.

units.label: Verse 1.1
units.deva:
बहिःप्रज्ञो विभुर्विश्वो ह्यन्तःप्रज्ञस्तु तैजसः।
घनप्रज्ञस्तथा प्राज्ञ एक एव त्रिधा स्थितः॥
units.translation: Viśva is all-pervading, the experiencer of external objects. Taijasa is the cognizer of internal objects. Prājña is a mass of consciousness. It is one alone that is thus known in the three states.

units.label: Verse 1.2
units.deva:
दक्षिणाक्षिमुखे विश्वो मनस्यन्तस्तु तैजसः।
आकाशे च हृदि प्राज्ञस्त्रिधा देहे व्यवस्थितः॥
units.translation: Viśva is the cognizer through the right eye; Taijasa is the cognizer through the mind within; Prājña is the ākāśa in the heart. Therefore the one Ātman is perceived threefold in the same body.

units.label: Verses 1.3–1.4
units.deva:
विश्वो हि स्थूलभुङ् नित्यं तैजसः प्रविविक्तभुक्।
आनन्दभुक्तथा प्राज्ञस्त्रिधा भोगं निबोधत॥
स्थूलं तर्पयते विश्वं प्रविविक्तं तु तैजसम्।
आनन्दश्च तथा प्राज्ञं त्रिधा तृप्तिं निबोधत॥
units.translation: Always, Viśva experiences the gross; Taijasa, the subtle; and Prājña, the blissful. Know these to be the threefold experience. The gross object satisfies Viśva; the subtle, Taijasa; and the blissful, Prājña. Know these to be the threefold satisfaction.

units.label: Verse 1.5
units.deva:
त्रिषु धामसु यद्भोज्यं भोक्ता यश्च प्रकीर्तितः।
वेदैतदुभयं यस्तु स भुञ्जानो न लिप्यते॥
units.translation: The experiencer and the objects of experience associated with the three states have been described. He who knows these both does not become attached to objects though enjoying them.

units.label: Verse 1.6
units.deva:
प्रभवः सर्वभावानां सतामिति विनिश्चयः।
सर्वं जनयति प्राणश्चेतोंशून्पुरुषः पृथक्॥
units.translation: Surely a coming into existence must be predicated of all positive entities that exist. Prāṇa manifests all objects. The Puruṣa manifests the conscious beings in their manifold forms.

units.label: Verse 1.7
units.deva:
विभूतिं प्रसवं त्वन्ये मन्यन्ते सृष्टिचिन्तकाः।
स्वप्नमायासरूपेति सृष्टिरन्यैर्विकल्पिता॥
units.translation: Some of those who contemplate the process of creation regard it as the manifestation of God’s powers; others imagine creation to be like dreams and illusions.

units.label: Verse 1.8
units.deva:
इच्छामात्रं प्रभोः सृष्टिरिति सृष्टौ विनिश्चिताः।
कालात्प्रसूतिं भूतानां मन्यन्ते कालचिन्तकाः॥
units.translation: Those who are convinced about the reality of manifested objects ascribe the manifestation solely to God’s will, while those who speculate about time regard time as the creator of things.

units.label: Verse 1.9
units.deva:
भोगार्थं सृष्टिरित्यन्ये क्रीडार्थमिति चापरे।
देवस्यैष स्वभावोऽयम् आप्तकामस्य का स्पृहा॥
units.translation: Some say that the manifestation is for the purpose of God’s enjoyment, while others attribute it to His diversion. But it is the very nature of the effulgent Being. What desire is possible for Him who is the fulfilment of all desires?

units.label: Verse 1.10
units.deva:
निवृत्तेः सर्वदुःखानामीशानः प्रभुरव्ययः।
अद्वैतः सर्वभावानां देवस्तुर्यो विभुः स्मृतः॥
units.translation: Turīya, the changeless Ruler, is capable of destroying all miseries. All other entities being unreal, the non-dual Turīya alone is known as effulgent and all-pervading.

units.label: Verse 1.11
units.deva:
कार्यकारणबद्धौ ताविष्येते विश्वतैजसौ।
प्राज्ञः कारणबद्धस्तु द्वौ तौ तुर्ये न सिध्यतः॥
units.translation: Viśva and Taijasa are conditioned by cause and effect. Prājña is conditioned by cause alone. Neither cause nor effect exists in Turīya.

units.label: Verse 1.12
units.deva:
नात्मानं न परं चैव न सत्यं नापि चानृतम्।
प्राज्ञः किञ्चन संवेत्ति तुर्यं तत्सर्वदृक्सदा॥
units.translation: Prājña does not know anything of self or non-self, of truth or untruth. But Turīya is ever existent and all-seeing (of the Prājña and all else).

units.label: Verse 1.13
units.deva:
द्वैतस्याग्रहणं तुल्यमुभयोः प्राज्ञतुर्ययोः।
बीजनिद्रायुतः प्राज्ञः सा च तुर्ये न विद्यते॥
units.translation: Non-cognition of duality is common to both Prājña and Turīya. But Prājña is associated with sleep in the form of cause and this sleep does not exist in Turīya.

units.label: Verse 1.14
units.deva:
स्वप्ननिद्रायुतावाद्यौ प्राज्ञस्त्वस्वप्ननिद्रया।
न निद्रां नैव च स्वप्नं तुर्ये पश्यन्ति निश्चिताः॥
units.translation: The first two, Viśva and Taijasa, are associated with dreaming (wrong cognition) and sleep respectively; Prājña, with Sleep bereft of dreams. Knowers of Brahman see neither sleep nor dreams in Turīya.

units.label: Verse 1.15
units.deva:
अन्यथा गृह्णतः स्वप्नो निद्रा तत्त्वमजानतः।
विपर्यासे तयोः क्षीणे तुरीयं पदमश्नुते॥
units.translation: Dreaming is the wrong cognition and sleep the non-cognition, of Reality. When the erroneous knowledge in these two is destroyed, Turīya (Reality) is realized (is rightly understood).

units.label: Verse 1.16
units.deva:
अनादिमायया सुप्तो यदा जीवः प्रबुध्यते।
अजमनिद्रमस्वप्नमद्वैतं बुध्यते तदा॥
units.translation: When the jīva, asleep under the influence of beginningless māyā, is awakened, it then realizes birthless, sleepless and dreamless Non-duality.

units.label: Verse 1.17
units.deva:
प्रपञ्चो यदि विद्येत निवर्तेत न संशयः।
मायामात्रमिदं द्वैतमद्वैतं परमार्थतः॥
units.translation: If the phenomenal universe were (separately) real, then certainly it could disappear. The universe of duality which is cognized is mere illusion (māyā, is unreal); Non-duality alone is (and always was) the Supreme Reality.

units.label: Verse 1.18
units.deva:
विकल्पो विनिवर्तेत कल्पितो यदि केनचित्।
उपदेशादयं वादो ज्ञाते द्वैतं न विद्यते॥
units.translation: If anyone imagines illusory ideas such as the teacher, the taught and the scriptures, then they will disappear. These ideas (vikalpaḥ vādaḥ) are only for the purpose of instruction (upadeśa). Duality ceases to exist when Reality is known.

units.label: Verse 1.19
units.deva:
विश्वस्यात्वविवक्षायाम् आदिसामान्यमुत्कटम्।
मात्रासम्प्रतिपत्तौ स्यादाप्तिसामान्यमेव च॥
units.translation: When it is desired to describe Viśva as of the same nature as the letter A, evident is their commonality of being the first (ādi), the identity with the letter A being admitted. And also is the commonality of being all-pervasive (āpti).

units.label: Verse 1.20
units.deva:
तैजसस्योत्वविज्ञान उत्कर्षो दृश्यते स्फुटम्।
मात्रासम्प्रतिपत्तौ स्यादुभयत्वं तथाविधम्॥
units.translation: When understanding Taijasa as of the same nature as the letter U, evident is seen it being superior (utkarṣa), the identity with the letter U being admitted. In the same way is it being in the middle (ubhayatva).

units.label: Verse 1.21
units.deva:
मकारभावे प्राज्ञस्य मानसामान्यमुत्कटम्।
मात्रासम्प्रतिपत्तौ तु लयसामान्यमेव च॥
units.translation: When understanding Prājña as of the same nature as the letter M, evident is its commonality of being a measure (māna), the identity with the letter M being admitted. And also is the commonality of being a mergence (laya).

units.label: Verse 1.22
units.deva:
त्रिषु धामसु यस्तुल्यं सामान्यं वेत्ति निश्चितः।
स पूज्यः सर्वभूतानां वन्द्यश्चैव महामुनिः॥
units.translation: He who knows for certain the same common features among the three states and the three letters of Om, is worshipped and adored by all beings, and also is a great sage.

units.label: Verse 1.23
units.deva:
अकारो नयते विश्वमुकारश्चापि तैजसम्।
मकारश्च पुनः प्राज्ञं नामात्रे विद्यते गतिः॥
units.translation: (Meditation) on A leads one to Viśva, on U to Taijasa, and on M to Prājña. On the soundless (a-mātra of Om, being Turīya) there is no reaching.

units.label: Verse 1.24
units.deva:
ओङ्कारं पादशो विद्यात्पादा मात्रा न संशयः।
ओङ्कारं पादशो ज्ञात्वा न किञ्चिदपि चिन्तयेत्॥
units.translation: Om should be known quarter by quarter. There is no doubt that the quarters are the same as the letters. Having understood Om quarter by quarter, one should not think of (not pursue) anything else.

units.label: Verse 1.25
units.deva:
युञ्जीत प्रणवे चेतः प्रणवो ब्रह्म निर्भयम्।
प्रणवे नित्ययुक्तस्य न भयं विद्यते क्वचित्॥
units.translation: The mind should be concentrated on Om. Om is the fearless Brahman. He who is always absorbed in Om knows no fear whatever.

units.label: Verse 1.26
units.deva:
प्रणवो ह्यपरं ब्रह्म प्रणवश्च परं स्मृतः।
अपूर्वोऽनन्तरोऽबाह्योऽनपरः प्रणवोऽव्ययः॥
units.translation: Om is verily the Lower Brahman. It is also stated to be the Higher Brahman. Om is beginningless and unique. There is nothing outside it. It is unrelated to any (Lower) effect and is immutable.

units.label: Verse 1.27
units.deva:
सर्वस्य प्रणवो ह्यादिर्मध्यमन्तस्तथैव च।
एवं हि प्रणवं ज्ञात्वा व्यश्नुते तदनन्तरम्॥
units.translation: Om is, indeed, the beginning, middle and end of all things. He who has realized Om as such immediately attains the Supreme Reality.

units.label: Verse 1.28
units.deva:
प्रणवं हीश्वरं विद्यात्सर्वस्य हृदये स्थितम्।
सर्वव्यापिनमोंकारं मत्वा धीरो न शोचति॥
units.translation: Know Om to be Īśvara, ever present in the hearts of all. The wise one, contemplating Om as all-pervading, does not grieve.

units.label: Verse 1.29
units.deva:
अमात्रोऽनन्तमात्रश्च द्वैतस्योपशमः शिवः।
ओङ्कारो विदितो येन स मुनिर्नेतरो जनः॥
units.translation: One who knows Om, which is soundless and also endowed with infinite sounds, which is all good and the negation of duality, is a real sage and anyone else is not.

units.label: Verse 2.1
units.deva:
वैतथ्यं सर्वभावानां स्वप्न आहुर्मनीषिणः।
अन्तःस्थानात्तु भावानां संवृतत्वेन हेतुना॥
units.translation: The wise declare the unreality of all entities seen in dreams, because they are located within the body and the space therein is confined.

units.label: Verse 2.2
units.deva:
अदीर्घत्वाच्च कालस्य गत्वा देहान्न पश्यति।
प्रतिबुद्धश्च वै सर्वस्तस्मिन्देशे न विद्यते॥
units.translation: The dreamer, on account of the shortness of the time involved, cannot go out of the body and see the dream objects. Nor does he, when awakened, find himself in the places seen in the dream.

units.label: Verse 2.3
units.deva:
अभावश्च रथादीनां श्रूयते न्यायपूर्वकम्।
वैतथ्यं तेन वै प्राप्तं स्वप्न आहुः प्रकाशितम्॥
units.translation: Scripture, on rational grounds, declares the non-existence of the chariots etc. perceived in dreams. Therefore the wise say that the unreality established by reason is proclaimed by scripture.

units.label: Verse 2.4
units.deva:
अन्तःस्थानात्तु भेदानां तस्माज्जागरिते स्मृतम्।
यथा तत्र तथा स्वप्ने संवृतत्वेन भिद्यते॥
units.translation: The different objects seen in the confined space of dreams are unreal on account of their being perceived. For the same reason i.e. on account of their being perceived, the objects seen in the waking state are also unreal. The same condition i.e. the state of being perceived exists in both waking and dreaming. The only difference is the limitation of space associated with dream objects.

units.label: Verse 2.5
units.deva:
स्वप्नजागरिते स्थाने ह्येकम् आहुर्मनीषिणः।
भेदानां हि समत्वेन प्रसिद्धेनैव हेतुना॥
units.translation: Thoughtful persons speak of the sameness of the waking and dream states on account of the similarity of the objects perceived in both states on the grounds already mentioned.

units.label: Verse 2.6
units.deva:
आदावन्ते च यन्नास्ति वर्तमानेऽपि तत्तथा।
वितथैः सदृशाः सन्तोऽवितथा इव लक्षिताः॥
units.translation: If a thing is non-existent both in the beginning and in the end, it is necessarily non-existent in the present. The objects that we see are really like illusions; still they are regarded as real.

units.label: Verse 2.7
units.deva:
सप्रयोजनता तेषां स्वप्ने विप्रतिपद्यते।
तस्मादाद्यन्तवत्त्वेन मिथ्यैव खलु ते स्मृताः॥
units.translation: The utility of the objects of waking experience is contradicted in dreams; therefore they are certainly unreal. Thus both experiences, having a beginning and an end, are unreal.

units.label: Verse 2.8
units.deva:
अपूर्वं स्थानिधर्मो हि यथा स्वर्गनिवासिनाम्।
तानयं प्रेक्षते गत्वा यथैवेह सुशिक्षितः॥
units.translation: The objects perceived by the dreamer, not usually seen in the waking state, owe their existence to the peculiar conditions under which the cognizer i.e. the mind functions for the time being, as with those residing in heaven. The dreamer, associating himself with the dream conditions, perceives those objects, even as a man, well instructed here, goes from one place to another and sees the peculiar objects belonging to those places.

units.label: Verse 2.9
units.deva:
स्वप्नवृत्तावपि त्वन्तश्चेतसा कल्पितं त्वसत्।
बहिश्चेतोगृहीतं सद्दृष्टं वैतथ्यमेतयोः॥
units.translation: In dreams, what is imagined within the mind is illusory and what is cognized outside by the mind, real; but truly, both are known to be unreal.

units.label: Verse 2.10
units.deva:
जाग्रद्वृत्तावपि त्वन्तश्चेतसा कल्पितं त्वसत्।
बहिश्चेतोगृहीतं सद्युक्तं वैतथ्यमेतयोः॥
units.translation: Similarly, in the waking state, what is imagined within by the mind is illusory and what is cognized outside by the mind, real; but both should be held, on rational grounds, to be unreal.

units.label: Verse 2.11
units.deva:
उभयोरपि वैतथ्यं भेदानां स्थानयोर्यदि।
क एतान्बुध्यते भेदान्को वै तेषां विकल्पकः॥
units.translation: If the objects perceived in both waking and dreaming are illusory, who perceives all these objects and who, again, imagines them?

units.label: Verse 2.12
units.deva:
कल्पयत्यात्मनात्मानमात्मा देवः स्वमायया।
स एव बुध्यते भेदानिति वेदान्तनिश्चयः॥
units.translation: It is the self-luminous Ātman who, through the power of Its own māyā, imagines in Itself by Itself all the objects that the subject experiences within and without. It alone is the cognizer of objects. This is the decision of Vedānta.

units.label: Verse 2.13
units.deva:
विकरोत्यपरान्भावानन्तश्चित्ते व्यवस्थितान्।
नियतांश्च बहिश्चित्त एवं कल्पयते प्रभुः॥
units.translation: The Lord (Ātman), with His mind turned outward, imagines in diverse forms various objects either permanent, such as the earth, or impermanent, such as lightning, which are already in His mind in the form of vāsanas, or desires. Again, He turns His mind within and imagines various ideas.

units.label: Verse 2.14
units.deva:
चित्तकाला हि येऽन्तस्तु द्वयकालाश्च ये बहिः।
कल्पिता एव ते सर्वे विशेषो नान्यहेतुकः॥
units.translation: Those that are cognized internally only as long as the thought of them lasts and those that are perceived outside and relate to two points in time, are all mere objects of the imagination. There is no ground for differentiating the one from the other.

units.label: Verse 2.15
units.deva:
अव्यक्ता एव येऽन्तस्तु स्फुटा एव च ये बहिः।
कल्पिता एव ते सर्वे विशेषस्त्विन्द्रियान्तरे॥
units.translation: Those that exist within the mind as subjective ideas and are known as unmanifested and those that are perceived to exist outside in a manifested form, both are mere objects of the imagination. Their difference lies only in the difference of the organs by means of which they are perceived.

units.label: Verse 2.16
units.deva:
जीवं कल्पयते पूर्वं ततो भावान्पृथग्विधान्।
बाह्यानाध्यात्मिकांश्चैव यथाविद्यस्तथास्मृतिः॥
units.translation: First of all is imagined the jīva, the embodied individual and then are imagined the various entities, both external such as sounds, forms, etc. and internal such as the prāṇas, sense-organs, etc., that are perceived to exist. As is one’s knowledge so is one’s memory.

units.label: Verse 2.17
units.deva:
अनिश्चिता यथा रज्जुरन्धकारे विकल्पिता।
सर्पधारादिभिर्भावैस्तद्वदात्मा विकल्पितः॥
units.translation: As a rope lying in darkness, about whose nature one remains uncertain, is imagined to be a snake or a line of water, so Ātman is imagined in various ways.

units.label: Verse 2.18
units.deva:
निश्चितायां यथा रज्ज्वां विकल्पो विनिवर्तते।
रज्जुरेवेति चाद्वैतं तद्वदात्मविनिश्चयः॥
units.translation: When the real nature of the rope is ascertained, all misconceptions about it disappear and there arises the conviction that it is nothing but a rope. Even so is the true nature of Ātman determined.

units.label: Verse 2.19
units.deva:
प्राणादिभिरनन्तैस्तु भावैरेतैर्विकल्पितः।
मायैषा तस्य देवस्य ययायं मोहितः स्वयम्॥
units.translation: Ātman is imagined as prāṇa and other numberless ideas. All this is due to māyā, belonging to the effulgent Ātman, by which It appears, Itself, to be deluded.

units.label: Verses 2.20–2.28
units.deva:
प्राण इति प्राणविदो भूतानीति च तद्विदः।
गुणा इति गुणविदस्तत्त्वानीति च तद्विदः॥
पादा इति पादविदो विषया इति तद्विदः।
लोका इति लोकविदो देवा इति च तद्विदः॥
वेदा इति वेदविदो यज्ञा इति च तद्विदः।
भोक्तेति च भोक्तृविदो भोज्यमिति च तद्विदः॥
सूक्ष्म इति सूक्ष्मविदः स्थूल इति च तद्विदः।
मूर्त इति मूर्तविदोऽमूर्त इति च तद्विदः॥
काल इति कालविदो दिश इति च तद्विदः।
वादा इति वादविदो भुवनानीति तद्विदः॥
मन इति मनोविदो बुद्धिरिति च तद्विदः।
चित्तमिति चित्तविदो धर्माधर्मौ च तद्विदः॥
पञ्चविंशक इत्येके षड्विंश इति चापरे।
एकत्रिंशक इत्याहुरनन्त इति चापरे॥
लोकांल्लोकविदः प्राहुराश्रमा इति तद्विदः।
स्त्रीपुंनपुंसकं लैङ्गाः परापरमथापरे॥
सृष्टिरिति सृष्टिविदो लय इति च तद्विदः।
स्थितिरिति स्थितिविदः सर्वे चेह तु सर्वदा॥
units.translation: 20. Those (Those – e.g., the Vaiśeṣikas and the worshippers of Hiraṇya garbha, etc.) conversant with prāṇa (Prāṇa – They hold Prāṇa, i.e., Hiraṇya-garbha or extra-cosmic God, to be the cause of the universe. This is mere imagination of the mind. There is no rational proof of the reality of an extra-cosmic God or Person as the cause of the world.) describe Ātman as prāṇa; those (Those, etc. – e.g., the Cārvākas or the atheists.) conversant with the elements, as the elements (Bhūtas – They designate the four elements, such as, earth, water, fire and air, which are directly perceived by them, as the cause of the universe. The insentient elements cannot be the cause of the sentient beings. Therefore, this theory also is an imagination.); those (Those, etc. – e.g., the Sāṅkhyas.) conversant with the guṇas, as the guṇas (Guṇas – According to the Sāṅkhyas, the state of equilibrium of the three Guṇas, viz., Sattva, Rajas and Tamas, produces Mahat, etc., and through them the universe. This is also mere idea.); and those (Those, etc. – i.e., the Śaivas.) conversant with the tattvas, as the tattvas (Tattvas – The Śaivas enumerate three Tattvas or categories, viz., Ātmā, Avidyā and Śiva as the cause of the universe. This is also an imagination and hence untenable. For, Śiva being an entity separated from Ātman (from oneself), becomes an object like a pot, etc.). 21. Those acquainted with the pādas (Quarters – e.g., Viśva, Taijasa and Prājña. Ātman, being, without parts and also unrelated, cannot be really divided into quarters or parts.) call It the pādas; those (Those, etc. – i.e., thinkers like Vātsyāyana, etc.) acquainted with objects, the objects (Objects – Such as, sound, colour, etc., i.e., the objects perceived by the different sense-organs. The objects, on account of their changeable and negatable nature, cannot be the Ultimate Reality.); those (Those, etc. – i.e., the Paurāṇikas or the believers in Mythology.) acquainted with the lokas, the lokas (Lokas – Such as Bhūh, Bhuvaḥ and Svaḥ. These being three in number are limited.); those (Those, etc. – i.e., the Karma Mimāṃsakas or the believers in the Karma portions of the Vedas.)those acquainted with the gods, the gods (Devas – Such as Agni (Fire), Indra, etc. According to this theory, Agni, Indra, etc., the various conscious deities, though not occupying the actual position of God (Īśvara), apportion the results of our various works. The conception of a separate God is not necessary. They cannot be the Ultimate Reality.). 22. Those conversant with the Vedas describe Ātman as the Vedas (Vedas – e.g., the four Vedas, Rig, Yajus, Sāma and Atharva. These Vedas cannot be the Ultimate Reality inasmuch as they are sounds.); those (Those, etc. – i.e., sages such as Bodhāyana and others who are adept in the performance of sacrifices.) conversant with the sacrifices, as the sacrifices (Sacrifices – The upholders of sacrifices and rituals like the Yagnas think that sacrifices, such as Jyotiṣṭoma, etc., constitute the Highest Reality. But this is also an illusion. For, according to them, the sacrifice signifies the object (offered), the deity and the act of offering. Any one of these, singly, does not constitute sacrifice. Again three of them, combined together, do not constitute any real entity.); those (Those, etc. – viz., the Sāṅkhyas.) conversant with the enjoyer, as the enjoyer (Enjoyer – According to the Sāṅkhyas the Ultimate Reality as the Puruṣa who is not the agent or doer but a mere enjoyer. This theory is not rational, for enjoyment means some change in the enjoyer which thus Contradicts the idea of his being eternal and changeless. If enjoyment be predicated as the inherent nature of Puruṣa, then the conception of extraneous objects, conducive to its enjoyments, is inconsistent.); and those (Those, etc. – That is, the cook, to whom the only reality appears to be delicious dishes.) conversant with the objects of enjoyment call It the objects of enjoyment. 23. The knowers (Knowers – i.e., those who believe (or take) the Ātman to be subtle like an atom.) of the subtle call It the subtle (Subtle – This theory is irrational: for, we feel consciousness simultaneously all over the body.) and the knowers (Knowers – A sect of materialists who believe the gross body to be real.) of the gross, the gross (Gross – The gross body cannot be the Ultimate Reality as a dead or sleeping man, in spite of the body being in existence, is unconscious. Any single limb of the body is insentient. Therefore even their aggregate cannot constitute the conscious Reality.). Those (Those, etc. – i.e., the Āgamikas who believe a person, e.g., Śiva with a trident or Viṣṇu with a disc, to be the Ultimate Reality. These are also imaginary.) that are familiar with the Personal Deity call It the Personal Deity (Personal Deity – This is also an illusion.) and those (Those, etc. – i.e., The Buddhist ritualists.) that are familiar with the void, the void (Void – The idea that the Ultimate Reality is an absolute void is also an illusion, as a void also should have a knower, and so cannot be the substratum of the positive fact of the empirical universe.). 24. Those (Those, etc., – Such as the astrologers (astronomers).) that know time call Ātman time (Time – This theory is also fallacious as time is divided into various parts as moment, minute, hour, etc. Time is also an object (thought) of the perceiving mind.) and those that know space call It space. Those versed in the art of disputation call It the object of dispute; and those knowing the worlds call It the worlds (Worlds – This is also an illusory conception.). 25. The knowers (Cognisers, etc. – i.e., a sect of the materialists.) of the mind call Ātman the mind (Mind – This theory is also not tenable as mind is also an object, an instrument of the perceiving ego.); the knowers (Of, etc. – They are a class of Buddhists.) of the buddhi, the buddhi (Buddhi – This is also a wrong view of the Reality, as the functionings of Buddhi disappear at the time of deep sleep. Further Buddhi is also an object cognized by the perceiver.). The knowers of the citta call It the citta (Citta – Citta is an aspect of mind which has no particular external form. It cannot be Ātman for the reasons given regarding mind.); and the knowers (Knowers, etc. – i.e., the Mimāṃsakas.) of righteousness and unrighteousness call (The one, etc. – None of these can be the Ultimate Reality because one cannot be conceived without the other and they have no absolute standard. They vary with different conditions of time and country.) It righteousness and unrighteousness. Some (Some – i.e., the Sāṅkhyas according to whom the Reality consists of twenty-five categories, viz., Prakṛti, Mahat, Ahaṅkāra, five Tan-mātras (subtle elements), five organs of perception, five organs of action, five objects, mind and the Puruṣa.) say that Ātman consists of twenty-five cosmic principles; some (Others – i.e., the followers of Patañjali who add Īśvara to the categories of the Sāṅkhyas.), of twenty-six principles; some (Others – i.e., the Pāsu-patas who add to the categories of Sāṅkhyas six more, viz., Rāga, Avidyā, Kāla, Kalā, Māyā and Niyati.), again, of thirty-one principles; while there are yet others who describe It as consisting of an infinite number of principles. Comment (The mutual contradictions among these different schools prove the fallacious character of their theories. The difference of opinion is due to the ignorance of the nature of Reality.). 27. Those (Those, etc. – i.e., a sect of the atheists.) who know how to gratify others call Ātman gratification (Such, etc. – This is also a delusion as it is impossible to please everybody on account of the different tastes of the people.); those (Those, etc. – i.e., men like Dakṣa, etc.) who are conversant with the āśramas call It the āśramas. The grammarians call It the masculine, feminine and neuter genders; and still others, the Higher (Parā, etc. – i.e., the Brahman who is regarded as high and low. An entity, subject to division of any sort, can never be the Supreme Reality.) Brahman and the Lower Brahman. 28. The knowers (Knowers, etc. – i.e., the Paurāṇikas (the believers in Mythology) who believe in the reality of creation, preservation and destruction.) of creation call It creation; the knowers of dissolution, dissolution; and the knowers of preservation, preservation. In truth, all such (All such – i.e., those enumerated above and which may be enumerated by others in future.) ideas are always imagined (Imagined – So long as men are given to imagining, they have recourse to all such imaginations regarding Ātman. But Ātman, from its own standpoint, does not imagine anything. It is because all these ideas, described above, are mere imaginations, that they cannot be the underlying Reality.) in Ātman.

units.label: Verse 2.29
units.deva:
यं भावं दर्शयेद्यस्य तं भावं स तु पश्यति।
तं चावति स भूत्वासौ तद्ग्रहः समुपैति तम्॥
units.translation: The disciple grasps only that idea which is presented to him by his teacher. Ātman assumes the form of what is taught and thus protects the disciple. Absorbed in that idea, he realizes it as Ātman.

units.label: Verse 2.30
units.deva:
एतैरेषोऽपृथग्भावैः पृथगेवेति लक्षितः।
एवं यो वेद तत्त्वेन कल्पयेत्सोऽविशङ्कितः॥
units.translation: Ātman, though non-separate from all these ideas, appears to he separate. He who truly knows this interprets, without any fear, the meaning of the Vedas.

units.label: Verse 2.31
units.deva:
स्वप्नमाये यथा दृष्टे गन्धर्वनगरं यथा।
तथा विश्वमिदं दृष्टं वेदान्तेषु विचक्षणैः॥
units.translation: As dreams, illusions and castles in the air are viewed, so is the tangible universe viewed by the wise, well versed in Vedānta.

units.label: Verse 2.32
units.deva:
न निरोधो न चोत्पत्तिर्न बद्धो न च साधकः।
न मुमुक्षुर्न वै मुक्त इत्येषा परमार्थता॥
units.translation: There is neither dissolution nor creation, none in bondage and none practicing disciplines. There is none seeking Liberation and none liberated. This is the absolute truth.

units.label: Verse 2.33
units.deva:
भावैरसद्भिरेवायमद्वयेन च कल्पितः।
भावा अप्यद्वयेनैव तस्मादद्वयता शिवा॥
units.translation: Ātman is imagined as the unreal objects that are perceived to exist and as Non-duality as well. The objects, too, are imagined in the non-dual Ātman. Therefore Non-duality is Bliss.

units.label: Verse 2.34
units.deva:
नात्मभावेन नानेदं न स्वेनापि कथञ्चन।
न पृथङ् नापृथक्किंचिदिति तत्त्वविदो विदुः॥
units.translation: The diversity in the universe does not exist as an entity identical With Ātman, nor does it exist by itself. Neither is it separate from Brahman nor is it non-separate. This is the statement of the wise.

units.label: Verse 2.35
units.deva:
वीतरागभयक्रोधैर्मुनिभिर्वेदपारगैः।
निर्विकल्पो ह्ययं दृष्टः प्रपञ्चोपशमोऽद्वयः॥
units.translation: The wise, who are free from attachment, fear and anger and are well versed in the Vedas, have realized Ātman as devoid of all phantasms and free from the illusion of the manifold and as non-dual.

units.label: Verse 2.36
units.deva:
तस्मादेवं विदित्वैनमद्वैते योजयेत्स्मृतिम्।
अद्वैतं समनुप्राप्य जडवल्लोकम् आचरेत्॥
units.translation: Therefore, knowing Ātman as such, fix your attention on Non-duality. Having realized Non-duality, behave in the world like an inert object.

units.label: Verse 2.37
units.deva:
निःस्तुतिर्निर्नमस्कारो निःस्वधाकार एव च।
चलाचलनिकेतश्च यतिर्यादृच्छिको भवेत्॥
units.translation: The illumined sannyāsin does not praise any deity, does not salute any superior and does not perform rites to propitiate departed ancestors. Regarding both body and Ātman as his abode, he remains satisfied with what comes by chance.

units.label: Verse 2.38
units.deva:
तत्त्वम् आध्यात्मिकं दृष्ट्वा तत्त्वं दृष्ट्वा तु बाह्यतः।
तत्त्वीभूतस्तदारामस्तत्त्वादप्रच्युतो भवेत्॥
units.translation: Having known the truth regarding what exists internally as also the truth regarding what exists externally, he becomes one with Reality, he exults in Reality and never deviates from Reality.

units.label: Verse 3.1
units.deva:
उपासनाश्रितो धर्मो जाते ब्रह्मणि वर्तते।
प्रागुत्पत्तेरजं सर्वं तेनासौ कृपणः स्मृतः॥
units.translation: The jīva, betaking himself to devotional worship, abides in the manifest Brahman. He thinks that before the creation all was of the same nature as the birthless Reality. Therefore he is said to possess a narrow intellect.

units.label: Verse 3.2
units.deva:
अतो वक्ष्याम्यकार्पण्यमजाति समतां गतम्।
यथा न जायते किञ्चिज्जायमानं समन्ततः॥
units.translation: Therefore I shall now describe Brahman, which is unborn, the same throughout and free from narrowness. From this one can understand that Brahman does not in reality pass into birth even in the slightest degree, though It appears to be manifest everywhere.

units.label: Verse 3.3
units.deva:
आत्मा ह्याकाशवज्जीवैर्घटाकाशैरिवोदितः।
घटादिवच्च सङ्घातैर्जातावेतन्निदर्शनम्॥
units.translation: Ātman, which is like ākāśa (infinite space), is said to be manifested in the form of jīvas, which may be likened to the ākāśas enclosed in pots. The bodies, also, are said to be manifested from Ātman, just as a pot and the like are created out of ākāśa. As regards the manifestation of Ātman this is the illustration.

units.label: Verse 3.4
units.deva:
घटादिषु प्रलीनेषु घटाकाशादयो यथा।
आकाशे सम्प्रलीयन्ते तद्वज्जीवा इहात्मनि॥
units.translation: As, on the destruction of the pot etc., the ākāśa enclosed in them merge in the great ākāśa, so the jīvas merge in Ātman.

units.label: Verse 3.5
units.deva:
यथैकस्मिन्घटाकाशे रजोधूमादिभिर्युते।
न सर्वे सम्प्रयुज्यन्ते तद्वज्जीवाः सुखादिभिः॥
units.translation: As the dust, smoke, etc. soiling the ākāśa enclosed in a particular pot do not soil the other ākāśas enclosed in other pots, so also the happiness, miseries, etc. of one jīva do not affect other jīvas.

units.label: Verse 3.6
units.deva:
रूपकार्यसमाख्याश्च भिद्यन्ते तत्र तत्र वै।
आकाशस्य न भेदोऽस्ति तद्वज्जीवेषु निर्णयः॥
units.translation: Though the diversity of forms, functions and names of the ākāśas associated with different receptacles is admitted, yet this does not imply any real differentiation in ākāśa itself. The same is the conclusion regarding the jīvas.

units.label: Verse 3.7
units.deva:
नाकाशस्य घटाकाशो विकारावयवौ यथा।
नैवात्मनः सदा जीवो विकारावयवौ तथा॥
units.translation: As the ākāśa enclosed in a pot is neither an effect nor a part of the real ākāśa, so the jīva is neither an effect nor a part of Ātman.

units.label: Verse 3.8
units.deva:
यथा भवति बालानां गगनं मलिनं मलैः।
तथा भवत्यबुद्धानाम् आत्मापि मलिनो मलैः॥
units.translation: Children regard ākāśa as being soiled by dirt; likewise the ignorant regard Ātman as being similarly soiled.

units.label: Verse 3.9
units.deva:
मरणे सम्भवे चैव गत्यागमनयोरपि।
स्थितौ सर्वशरीरेषु चाकाशेनाविलक्षणः॥
units.translation: Ātman, in regard to Its birth and death, Its going and coming i.e. rebirth and Its dwelling in different bodies, is not unlike ākāśa.

units.label: Verse 3.10
units.deva:
सङ्घाताः स्वप्नवत्सर्व आत्ममायाविसर्जिताः।
आधिक्ये सर्वसाम्ये वा नोपपत्तिर्हि विद्यते॥
units.translation: All aggregates are produced by Ātman’s māyā, as in a dream. No rational argument can be given to establish their reality, whether they are of equal status or whether some are superior to others.

units.label: Verse 3.11
units.deva:
रसादयो हि ये कोशा व्याख्यातास्तैत्तिरीयके।
तेषाम् आत्मा परो जीवः खं यथा सम्प्रकाशितः॥
units.translation: The Supreme Self is the self of the five sheaths, such as the physical and the vital, which have been described in the Taittirīya Upaniṣad. That the Supreme Self is like ākāśa has already been stated.

units.label: Verse 3.12
units.deva:
द्वयोर्द्वयोर्मधुज्ञाने परं ब्रह्म प्रकाशितम्।
पृथिव्यामुदरे चैव यथाकाशः प्रकाशितः॥
units.translation: The same ākāśa dwells within both the earth and the stomach; likewise, the same Brahman dwells within the pairs described in the Madhu-Brāhmaṇa.

units.label: Verse 3.13
units.deva:
जीवात्मनोरनन्यत्वमभेदेन प्रशस्यते।
नानात्वं निन्द्यते यच्च तदेवं हि समञ्जसम्॥
units.translation: The identity of the jīva and Ātman is praised by pointing out their non-duality; multiplicity is condemned. Therefore non-dualism alone is free from error.

units.label: Verse 3.14
units.deva:
जीवात्मनोः पृथक्त्वं यत्प्रागुत्पत्तेः प्रकीर्तितम्।
भविष्यद्वृत्त्या गौणं तन्मुख्यत्वं हि न युज्यते॥
units.translation: The separateness of the jīva and Ātman, which has been declared in the earlier section of the Upaniṣads, dealing with the creation, is figurative, because this section states only what will happen in the future. This separateness cannot be the real meaning of those passages.

units.label: Verse 3.15
units.deva:
मृल्लोहविस्फुलिङ्गाद्यैः सृष्टिर्या चोदितान्यथा।
उपायः सोऽवताराय नास्ति भेदः कथञ्चन॥
units.translation: The scriptural statements regarding the creation, using the examples of earth, iron and sparks, are for the purpose of clarifying the mind. Multiplicity does not really exist in any manner.

units.label: Verse 3.16
units.deva:
आश्रमास्त्रिविधा हीनमध्यमोत्कृष्टदृष्टयः।
उपासनोपदिष्टेयं तदर्थमनुकम्पया॥
units.translation: There are three stages of life, corresponding to the threefold understanding of men: inferior, mediocre and superior. Scripture, out of compassion, has taught this discipline for the benefit of the unenlightened.

units.label: Verse 3.17
units.deva:
स्वसिद्धान्तव्यवस्थासु द्वैतिनो निश्चिता दृढम्।
परस्परं विरुध्यन्ते तैरयं न विरुध्यते॥
units.translation: The dualists, firmly clinging to their conclusions, contradict one another. The non-dualists find no conflict with them.

units.label: Verse 3.18
units.deva:
अद्वैतं परमार्थो हि द्वैतं तद्भेद उच्यते।
तेषामुभयथा द्वैतं तेनायं न विरुध्यते॥
units.translation: Since Non-duality is Ultimate Reality, duality is said to be Its effect. The dualist sees duality in both the Absolute and the relative. Therefore the non-dualist position does not conflict with the dualist position.

units.label: Verse 3.19
units.deva:
मायया भिद्यते ह्येतन्नान्यथाजं कथञ्चन।
तत्त्वतो भिद्यमाने हि मर्त्यताममृतं व्रजेत्॥
units.translation: The unborn Ātman becomes manifold through māyā and not otherwise. For if the manifold were real, then the immortal would become mortal.

units.label: Verse 3.20
units.deva:
अजातस्यैव भावस्य जातिमिच्छन्ति वादिनः।
अजातो ह्यमृतो भावो मर्त्यतां कथमेष्यति॥
units.translation: The disputants assert that the unborn entity (Ātman) becomes born. Now can one expect that an entity that is birthless and immortal should become mortal?

units.label: Verse 3.21
units.deva:
न भवत्यमृतं मर्त्यं न मर्त्यममृतं तथा।
प्रकृतेरन्यथाभावो न कथञ्चिद्भविष्यति॥
units.translation: The immortal cannot become mortal, nor can the mortal become immortal. For it is never possible for a thing to change its nature.

units.label: Verse 3.22
units.deva:
स्वभावेनामृतो यस्य भावो गच्छति मर्त्यताम्।
कृतकेनामृतस्तस्य कथं स्थास्यति निश्चलः॥
units.translation: How can one who believes that an entity by nature immortal becomes mortal, maintain that the immortal, after passing through change, retains its changeless nature?

units.label: Verse 3.23
units.deva:
भूततोऽभूततो वापि सृज्यमाने समा श्रुतिः।
निश्चितं युक्तियुक्तं च यत्तद्भवति नेतरत्॥
units.translation: Coming into birth may be real or illusory; both views are equally supported by the scriptures. But that view which is supported by the scriptures and corroborated by reason is alone to be accepted and not the other.

units.label: Verse 3.24
units.deva:
नेह नानेति चाम्नायादिन्द्रो मायाभिरित्यपि।
अजायमानो बहुधा जायते मायया तु सः॥
units.translation: From such scriptural passages as, “One does not see any multiplicity in Ātman” and “Indra (the Supreme Lord), through māyā, assumes diverse forms”, one knows that Ātman, though ever unborn, appears to have become many only through māyā.

units.label: Verse 3.25
units.deva:
सम्भूतेरपवादाच्च सम्भवः प्रतिषिध्यते।
को न्वेनं जनयेदिति कारणं प्रतिषिध्यते॥
units.translation: Further, by the negation of the creation, coming into birth is negated. The causality of Brahman is denied by such a statement as “Who can cause It to come into birth?”

units.label: Verse 3.26
units.deva:
स एष नेति नेतीति व्याख्यातं निह्नुते यतः।
सर्वमग्राह्यभावेन हेतुनाजं प्रकाशते॥
units.translation: On account of the incomprehensible nature of Ātman, the scriptural passage “Not this, not this” negates all dualistic ideas attributed to Ātman. Therefore the birthless Ātman alone exists.

units.label: Verse 3.27
units.deva:
सतो हि मायया जन्म युज्यते न तु तत्त्वतः।
तत्त्वतो जायते यस्य जातं तस्य हि जायते॥
units.translation: What is ever existent appears to pass into birth through māyā, yet from the standpoint of Reality it does not do so. But he who thinks this passing into birth is real asserts, as a matter of fact, that what is born passes into birth again.

units.label: Verse 3.28
units.deva:
असतो मायया जन्म तत्त्वतो नैव युज्यते।
वन्ध्यापुत्रो न तत्त्वेन मायया वापि जायते॥
units.translation: The unreal cannot be born either really or through māyā. For it is not possible for the son of a barren woman to be born either really or through māyā.

units.label: Verse 3.29
units.deva:
यथा स्वप्ने द्वयाभासं स्पन्दते मायया मनः।
तथा जाग्रद्द्वयाभासं स्पन्दते मायया मनः॥
units.translation: As in dreams the mind acts through māyā, presenting the appearance of duality, so also in the waking state the mind acts through māyā, presenting the appearance of duality.

units.label: Verse 3.30
units.deva:
अद्वयं च द्वयाभासं मनः स्वप्ने न संशयः।
अद्वयं च द्वयाभासं तथा जाग्रन्न संशयः॥
units.translation: There is no doubt that the mind, which is in reality non-dual, appears to be dual in dreams; likewise, there is no doubt that what is non-dual, i.e. Ātman, appears to be dual in the waking state.

units.label: Verse 3.31
units.deva:
मनोदृश्यमिदं द्वैतं यत्किञ्चित्सचराचरम्।
मनसो ह्यमनीभावे द्वैतं नैवोपलभ्यते॥
units.translation: All the multiple objects, comprising the movable and the immovable, are perceived by the mind alone. For duality is never perceived when the mind ceases to act.

units.label: Verse 3.32
units.deva:
आत्मसत्यानुबोधेन न सङ्कल्पयते यदा।
अमनस्तां तदा याति ग्राह्याभावे तदग्रहम्॥
units.translation: When the mind, after realizing the knowledge that Ātman alone is real, becomes free from imaginations and therefore does not cognize anything, for want of objects to he cognized, it ceases to be the mind.

units.label: Verse 3.33
units.deva:
अकल्पकमजं ज्ञानं ज्ञेयाभिन्नं प्रचक्षते।
ब्रह्म ज्ञेयमजं नित्यमजेनाजं विबुध्यते॥
units.translation: Knowledge (Jñāna), which is unborn and free from imagination, is described by the wise as ever inseparable from the knowable. The immutable and birthless Brahman is the goal of knowledge. The birthless is known by the birthless.

units.label: Verse 3.34
units.deva:
निगृहीतस्य मनसो निर्विकल्पस्य धीमतः।
प्रचारः स तु विज्ञेयः सुषुप्तेऽन्यो न तत्समः॥
units.translation: One should know the behaviour of the mind which, being endowed with discrimination and free from illusions is under control. The condition of the mind in deep sleep is not like that but is of a different kind.

units.label: Verse 3.35
units.deva:
लीयते हि सुषुप्तौ तन्निगृहीतं न लीयते।
तदेव निर्भयं ब्रह्म ज्ञानालोकं समन्ततः॥
units.translation: The mind is withdrawn in deep sleep, but it is not so when the mind is controlled. The controlled mind is verily the fearless Brahman, the light of whose omniscience is all-pervading.

units.label: Verse 3.36
units.deva:
अजमनिद्रमस्वप्नमनामकमरूपकम्।
सकृद्विभातं सर्वज्ञं नोपचारः कथञ्चन॥
units.translation: Brahman is birthless, sleepless, dreamless, nameless and formless. It is ever effulgent and omniscient. No duty, in any sense, can ever be associated with It.

units.label: Verse 3.37
units.deva:
सर्वाभिलापविगतः सर्वचिन्तासमुत्थितः।
सुप्रशान्तः सकृज्ज्योतिः समाधिरचलोऽभयः॥
units.translation: Ātman is beyond all expression by words and beyond all acts of the mind. It is great peace, eternal effulgence and samādhi; It is unmoving and fearless.

units.label: Verse 3.38
units.deva:
ग्रहो न तत्र नोत्सर्गश्चिन्ता यत्र न विद्यते।
आत्मसंस्थं तदा ज्ञानमजाति समतां गतम्॥
units.translation: Brahman is free from mental activity and hence from all ideas of acceptance or relinquishment. When knowledge is established in Ātman it attains birthlessness and sameness.

units.label: Verse 3.39
units.deva:
अस्पर्शयोगो वै नाम दुर्दर्शः सर्वयोगिणाम्।
योगिनो बिभ्यति ह्यस्मादभये भयदर्शिनः॥
units.translation: This yoga, which is not in touch with anything, is hard for yogīs in general to attain. They are afraid of it, because they see fear in that which is really fearlessness.

units.label: Verse 3.40
units.deva:
मनसो निग्रहायत्तमभयं सर्वयोगिणाम्।
दुःखक्षयः प्रबोधश्चाप्यक्षया शान्तिरेव च॥
units.translation: Yogīs who are ignorant of Non-duality depend on the control of the mind for attaining fearlessness, the destruction of misery, Self-Knowledge and imperishable peace.

units.label: Verse 3.41
units.deva:
उत्सेक उदधेर्यद्वत्कुशाग्रेणैकबिन्दुना।
मनसो निग्रहस्तद्वद्भवेदपरिखेदतः॥
units.translation: The mind is to be brought under Control by undepressed effort; it is like emptying the ocean, drop by drop, with the help of a blade of kuśa grass.

units.label: Verse 3.42
units.deva:
उपायेन निगृह्णीयाद्विक्षिप्तं कामभोगयोः।
सुप्रसन्नं लये चैव यथा कामो लयस्तथा॥
units.translation: The mind distracted by desires and enjoyments should he brought under control by proper means; so also the mind enjoying pleasure in inactivity (laya). For the state of inactivity is as harmful as the state of desires.

units.label: Verse 3.43
units.deva:
दुःखं सर्वमनुस्मृत्य कामभोगान्निवर्तयेत्।
अजं सर्वमनुस्मृत्य जातं नैव तु पश्यति॥
units.translation: Turn back the mind from the enjoyment of desires, remembering that they beget only misery. Do not see the created objects, remembering that all this is the unborn Ātman.

units.label: Verse 3.44
units.deva:
लये संबोधयेच्चित्तं विक्षिप्तं शमयेत्पुनः।
सकषायं विजानीयात्समप्राप्तं न चालयेत्॥
units.translation: If the mind becomes inactive, arouse it from laya; if distracted, make it tranquil. Understand the nature of the mind when it contains the seed of attachment. When the mind has attained sameness, do not disturb it again.

units.label: Verse 3.45
units.deva:
नास्वादयेत्सुखं तत्र निःसङ्गः प्रज्ञया भवेत्।
निश्चलं निश्चरच्चित्तमेकीकुर्यात्प्रयत्नतः॥
units.translation: The yogī must not taste the happiness arising from samādhi; he should detach himself from it by the exercise of discrimination. If his mind, after attaining steadiness, again seeks external objects, he should make it one with Ātman through great effort.

units.label: Verse 3.46
units.deva:
यदा न लीयते चित्तं न च विक्षिप्यते पुनः।
अनिङ्गनमनाभासं निष्पन्नं ब्रह्म तत्तदा॥
units.translation: When the mind does not lapse into inactivity and is not distracted by desires, that is to say, when it remains unshakable and does not give rise to appearances, it verily becomes Brahman.

units.label: Verse 3.47
units.deva:
स्वस्थं शान्तं सनिर्वाणमकथ्यं सुखमुत्तमम्।
अजमजेन ज्ञेयेन सर्वज्ञं परिचक्षते॥
units.translation: This Supreme Bliss abides in the Self. It is peace; it is Liberation; it is birthless and cannot be described in words. It is called the omniscient Brahman, being one with the birthless Self, which is the true object of knowledge.

units.label: Verse 3.48
units.deva:
न कश्चिज्जायते जीवः सम्भवोऽस्य न विद्यते।
एतत्तदुत्तमं सत्यं यत्र किञ्चिन्न जायते॥
units.translation: No jīva ever comes into existence. There exists no cause that can produce it. The supreme truth is that nothing ever is born.

units.label: Verse 4.1
units.deva:
ज्ञानेनाकाशकल्पेन धर्मान्यो गगनोपमान्।
ज्ञेयाभिन्नेन संबुद्धस्तं वन्दे द्विपदां वरम्॥
units.translation: I bow to the best among men, who, by means of knowledge, which is like ākāśa and which is non-different from the goal of knowledge, realized the nature of the jīvas (dharmas), which, too, are like ākāśa.

units.label: Verse 4.2
units.deva:
अस्पर्शयोगो वै नाम सर्वसत्त्वसुखो हितः।
अविवादोऽविरुद्धश्च देशितस्तं नमाम्यहम्॥
units.translation: I bow to the yoga known as a-sparśa, taught in the scriptures, which promotes the happiness and well-being of all creatures and is free from strife and contradictions.

units.label: Verse 4.3
units.deva:
भूतस्य जातिमिच्छन्ति वादिनः केचिदेव हि।
अभूतस्यापरे धीरा विवदन्तः परस्परम्॥
units.translation: Some disputants postulate that only an existing entity can again come into existence, while other disputants, proud of their intellect, postulate that only a non-existing entity can come into existence. Thus they quarrel among themselves.

units.label: Verse 4.4
units.deva:
भूतं न जायते किञ्चिदभूतं नैव जायते।
विवदन्तोऽद्वया ह्येवमजातिं ख्यापयन्ति ते॥
units.translation: An existing entity cannot again come into existence (birth); nor can a non-existing entity come into existence. Thus disputing among themselves, they really establish the non-dualistic view of a-jāti (non-creation).

units.label: Verse 4.5
units.deva:
ख्याप्यमानामजातिं तैरनुमोदामहे वयम्।
विवदामो न तैः सार्धमविवादं निबोधत॥
units.translation: We approve the a-jāti (non-creation) thus established by them. We have no quarrel with them. Now hear from us about Ultimate Reality, which is free from all disputations.

units.label: Verse 4.6
units.deva:
अजातस्यैव धर्मस्य जातिमिच्छन्ति वादिनः।
अजातो ह्यमृतो धर्मो मर्त्यतां कथमेष्यति॥
units.translation: The disputants assert that the unborn entity (Ātman) becomes born. How can one expect that an entity that is birthless and immortal should become mortal?

units.label: Verses 4.7–4.8
units.deva:
न भवत्यमृतं मर्त्यं न मर्त्यममृतं तथा।
प्रकृतेरन्यथाभावो न कथञ्चिद्भविष्यति॥
स्वभावेनामृतो यस्य धर्मो गच्छति मर्त्यतात्।
कृतकेनामृतस्तस्य कथं स्थास्यति निश्चलः॥
units.translation: 7. The immortal cannot become mortal, nor can the mortal become immortal. For it is never possible for a thing to change its nature. 8. How can one who believes that an entity by nature immortal becomes mortal, maintain that the immortal, after passing through change, retains its changeless nature?

units.label: Verse 4.9
units.deva:
सांसिद्धिकी स्वाभाविकी सहजा अकृता च या।
प्रकृतिः सेति विज्ञेया स्वभावं न जहाति या॥
units.translation: By the prakṛti, or nature, of a thing is understood that which, when acquired, becomes the essential part of the thing, that which is its characteristic quality, that which is its inalienable nature from its very birth, that which is not extraneous to it and that which never ceases to be itself.

units.label: Verse 4.10
units.deva:
जरामरणनिर्मुक्ताः सर्वे धर्माः स्वभावतः।
जरामरणमिच्छन्तश्च्यवन्ते तन्मनीषया॥
units.translation: All the jīvas are, by their very nature, free from senility and death. But they think they are subject to senility and death and by the very power of thought they appear to deviate from their true nature.

units.label: Verse 4.11
units.deva:
कारणं यस्य वै कार्यं कारणं तस्य जायते।
जायमानं कथमजं भिन्नं नित्यं कथं च तत्॥
units.translation: The disputant according to whom the cause itself is the effect must maintain that the cause is born as the effect. If it is born, how can it be called birthless? If it is subject to modification, how then can it be said to be eternal?

units.label: Verse 4.12
units.deva:
कारणाद्यद्यनन्यत्वमतः कार्यमजं तव।
जायमानाद्धि वै कार्यात्कारणं ते कथं ध्रुवम्॥
units.translation: If, as you say, the effect is non-different from the cause, then the effect too must be unborn. Further, how can the cause be eternal if it is non-different from the effect, which is born?

units.label: Verse 4.13
units.deva:
अजाद्वै जायते यस्य दृष्टान्तस्तस्य नास्ति वै।
जाताच्च जायमानस्य न व्यवस्था प्रसज्यते॥
units.translation: There is no illustration to support the view that the effect is born from an unborn cause. Again, if it is said that the effect is produced from a cause which itself is born, then this leads to an infinite regress.

units.label: Verse 4.14
units.deva:
हेतोरादिः फलं येषाम् आदिर्हेतुः फलस्य च।
हेतोः फलस्य चानादिः कथं तैरुपवर्ण्यते॥
units.translation: How can they who assert that the effect is the cause of the cause and the cause is the cause of the effect, maintain the beginninglessness of both cause and effect?

units.label: Verse 4.15
units.deva:
हेतोरादिः फलं येषाम् आदिर्हेतुः फलस्य च।
तथा जन्म भवेत्तेषां पुत्राज्जन्म पितुर्यथा॥
units.translation: Those who say that the effect is the cause of the cause and that the cause is the cause of the effect maintain, actually, that the creation takes place after the manner of the birth of father from son.

units.label: Verse 4.16
units.deva:
सम्भवे हेतुफलयोरेषितव्यः क्रमस्त्वया।
युगपत्संभवे यस्मादसम्बन्धो विषाणवत्॥
units.translation: If causality is asserted, then the order in which cause and effect succeed each other must be stated. If it is said that they appear simultaneously, then, being like the two horns of an animal, they cannot be mutually related as cause and effect.

units.label: Verse 4.17
units.deva:
फलादुत्पद्यमानः सन्न ते हेतुः प्रसिध्यति।
अप्रसिद्धः कथं हेतुः फलमुत्पादयिष्यति॥
units.translation: The cause that you affirm, cannot be established as the cause if it is produced from the effect. How can the cause, which itself is not established, give birth to the effect?

units.label: Verse 4.18
units.deva:
यदि हेतोः फलात्सिद्धिः फलसिद्धिश्च हेतुतः।
कतरत्पूर्वनिष्पन्नं यस्य सिद्धिरपेक्षया॥
units.translation: If the cause is produced from the effect and if the effect is, again, produced from the cause, which of the two is born first upon which depends the birth of the other?

units.label: Verse 4.19
units.deva:
अशक्तिरपरिज्ञानं क्रमकोपोऽथ वा पुनः।
एवं हि सर्वथा बुद्धैरजातिः परिदीपिता॥
units.translation: The inability to reply to the question raised above, the ignorance about the matter and the impossibility of establishing the order of succession if the causal relation is admitted clearly lead the wise to uphold, under all conditions, the doctrine of a-jāti, or non-creation.

units.label: Verse 4.20
units.deva:
बीजाङ्कुराख्यो दृष्टान्तः सदा साध्यसमो हि सः।
न हि साध्यसमो हेतुः सिद्धौ साध्यस्य युज्यते॥
units.translation: The illustration of the seed and the sprout is something which is yet to be proved. The illustration i.e. the middle term, which itself is not yet proved, cannot be used for establishing a proposition to be proved.

units.label: Verse 4.21
units.deva:
पूर्वापरापरिज्ञानमजातेः परिदीपकम्।
जायमानाद्धि वै धर्मात्कथं पूर्वं न गृह्यते॥
units.translation: The ignorance regarding the antecedence and the subsequence of cause and effect clearly proves the absence of creation (a-jāti). If the jīva (dharma) has really been born, then why can you not point out its antecedent cause?

units.label: Verse 4.22
units.deva:
स्वतो वा परतो वापि न किञ्चिद्वस्तु जायते।
सदसत् सदसद् वापि न किञ्चिद्वस्तु जायते॥
units.translation: Nothing whatsoever is born, either of itself or of another entity. Nothing is ever produced, whether it be being or non-being or both being and non-being.

units.label: Verse 4.23
units.deva:
हेतुर्न जायतेऽनादेः फलं चापि स्वभावतः।
आदिर्न विद्यते यस्य तस्य ह्यादिर्न विद्यते॥
units.translation: The cause cannot be produced from a beginningless effect; nor can the effect be produced from a beginningless cause. That which is without beginning is necessarily free from birth.

units.label: Verse 4.24
units.deva:
प्रज्ञप्तेः सनिमित्तत्वमन्यथा द्वयनाशतः।
संक्लेशस्योपलब्धेश्च परतन्त्रास्तिता मता॥
units.translation: Subjective knowledge must have an object for its cause; otherwise variety becomes non-existent. Further, from the experience of pain, the existence of external objects, accepted by the dualistic scriptures, must be admitted.

units.label: Verse 4.25
units.deva:
प्रज्ञप्तेः सनिमित्तत्वमिष्यते युक्तिदर्शनात्।
निमित्तस्यानिमित्तत्वमिष्यते भूतदर्शनात्॥
units.translation: The dualists, by force of reason, assert that there is a cause of subjective knowledge. But from the standpoint of the true nature of things we assert that the so-called cause is, after all, no cause.

units.label: Verse 4.26
units.deva:
चित्तं न संस्पृशत्यर्थं नार्थाभासं तथैव च।
अभूतो हि यतश्चार्थो नार्थाभासस्ततः पृथक्॥
units.translation: The mind is not related to external objects or to the ideas that appear as such objects. This is so because objects are non-existent and the ideas that appear as external objects are not distinct from the mind.

units.label: Verse 4.27
units.deva:
निमित्तं न सदा चित्तं संस्पृशत्यध्वसु त्रिषु।
अनिमित्तो विपर्यासः कथं तस्य भविष्यति॥
units.translation: The mind does not enter into the causal relation in any of the three periods of time. How can it ever be subject to delusion, when there is no cause for such delusion?

units.label: Verse 4.28
units.deva:
तस्मान्न जायते चित्तं चित्तदृश्यं न जायते।
तस्य पश्यन्ति ये जातिं खे वै पश्यन्ति ते पदम्॥
units.translation: Therefore neither the mind nor the objects perceived by the mind are ever born. To see their birth is like seeing the footprints of birds in the sky.

units.label: Verse 4.29
units.deva:
अजातं जायते यस्मादजातिः प्रकृतिस्ततः।
प्रकृतेरन्यथाभावो न कथञ्चिद्भविष्यति॥
units.translation: The cause, Brahman, from which the birthless mind is asserted, by the dualists, to have been born is itself unborn. Because Brahman is ever unborn, therefore it is never possible for It to be other than what It is.

units.label: Verse 4.30
units.deva:
अनादेरन्तवत्त्वं च संसारस्य न सेत्स्यति।
अनन्तता चादिमतो मोक्षस्य न भविष्यति॥
units.translation: If, as the dualists contend, the world is beginningless, then it cannot be non-eternal. Mokṣa (Liberation) cannot have a beginning and be eternal.

units.label: Verses 4.31–4.32
units.deva:
आदावन्ते च यन्नास्ति वर्तमानेऽपि तत्तथा।
वितथैः सदृशाः सन्तोऽवितथा इव लक्षिताः॥
सप्रयोजनता तेषां स्वप्ने विप्रतिपद्यते।
तस्मादाद्यन्तवत्त्वेन मिथ्यैव खलु ते स्मृताः॥
units.translation: 31. If a thing is non-existent in the beginning and in the end, it is necessarily non-existent in the present. The objects that we see are really like illusions; still they are regarded as real. 32. The utility of the objects of waking experience is contradicted in dreams; therefore they are certainly unreal. Both experiences have a beginning and an end.

units.label: Verse 4.33
units.deva:
सर्वे धर्मा मृषा स्वप्ने कायस्यान्तर्निदर्शनात्।
संवृतेऽस्मिन्प्रदेशे वै भूतानां दर्शनं कुतः॥
units.translation: All entities seen in dreams are unreal, because they are perceived inside the body. How is it possible for things that are perceived to exist, really to exist in Brahman, which is indivisible and homogeneous?

units.label: Verse 4.34
units.deva:
न युक्तं दर्शनं गत्वा कालस्यानियमाद्गतौ।
प्रतिबुद्धश्च वै सर्वस्तस्मिन्देशे न विद्यते॥
units.translation: It is not reasonable to think that a dreamer actually goes out in order to experience the objects seen in the dream, because of the discrepancy of the time involved in such a journey. Nor does he, when awakened, find himself in the places seen in the dream.

units.label: Verse 4.35
units.deva:
मित्राद्यैः सह संमन्त्र्य संबुद्धो न प्रपद्यते।
गृहीतं चापि यत्किञ्चित्प्रतिबुद्धो न पश्यति॥
units.translation: The dreamer, after awaking, realizes the illusoriness of the conversations he had with friends etc. in the dream state. Further, he does not possess in the waking state anything he acquired while dreaming.

units.label: Verse 4.36
units.deva:
स्वप्ने चावस्तुकः कायः पृथगन्यस्य दर्शनात्।
यथा कायस्तथा सर्वं चित्तदृश्यमवस्तुकम्॥
units.translation: The dream body is unsubstantial because the other i.e. the physical body, different from it, is perceived. Like the dream body, all things cognized by the mind are unsubstantial.

units.label: Verse 4.37
units.deva:
ग्रहणाज्जागरितवत्तद्धेतुः स्वप्न इष्यते।
तद्धेतुत्वात्तु तस्यैव सज्जागरितमिष्यते॥
units.translation: Since the experience of objects in dreams is similar to the experience of objects in the waking state, waking experience is regarded as the cause of dream experience. It is only by him who admits waking experience to be the cause of dream experience that waking experience can be regarded as real.

units.label: Verse 4.38
units.deva:
उत्पादस्याप्रसिद्धत्वादजं सर्वमुदाहृतम्।
न च भूतादभूतस्य सम्भवोऽस्ति कथञ्चन॥
units.translation: All entities are said to be unborn, since birth cannot be established as a fact. It is utterly impossible for the unreal to be born of the real.

units.label: Verse 4.39
units.deva:
असज्जागरिते दृष्ट्वा स्वप्ने पश्यति तन्मयः।
असत्स्वप्नेऽपि दृष्ट्वा च प्रतिबुद्धो न पश्यति॥
units.translation: A man filled with the impressions of the unreal objects seen in the waking state sees those very things in dreams as well. But he does not see in the waking state the unreal objects seen in dreams.

units.label: Verse 4.40
units.deva:
नास्त्यसद्धेतुकमसत्सदसद्धेतुकं तथा।
सच्च सद्धेतुकं नास्ति सद्धेतुकमसत्कुतः॥
units.translation: The unreal cannot have another unreality for its cause, nor can the real have the unreal for its cause. The real cannot be the cause of the real. And how utterly impossible it is for the real to be the cause of the unreal!

units.label: Verse 4.41
units.deva:
विपर्यासाद्यथा जाग्रदचिन्त्यान्भूतवत्स्पृशेत्।
तथा स्वप्ने विपर्यासाद्धर्मांस्तत्रैव पश्यति॥
units.translation: As a person in the waking state through false knowledge appears to handle objects, whose nature is inscrutable, as if they were real, so also, in dreams, he perceives, through false knowledge, objects whose existence is possible in the dream state alone.

units.label: Verse 4.42
units.deva:
उपलम्भात्समाचारादस्तिवस्तुत्ववादिनाम्।
जातिस्तु देशिता बुद्धैरजातेस्त्रसतां सदा॥
units.translation: Wise men teach causality only for the sake of those who, afraid of non-creation, assert the reality of external objects because they perceive such objects and also because they cling to various social and religious duties.

units.label: Verse 4.43
units.deva:
अजातेस्त्रसतां तेषामुपलम्भाद्वियन्ति ये।
जातिदोषा न सेत्स्यन्ति दोषोऽप्यल्पो भविष्यति॥
units.translation: Those who, because of their fear of the truth of absolute non-creation and also because of their perception of external objects, deny a-jāti (non-creation) are not affected by the evil consequent on the belief in creation. This evil, if there is any, is insignificant.

units.label: Verse 4.44
units.deva:
उपलम्भात्समाचारान्मायाहस्ती यथोच्यते।
उपलम्भात्समाचारादस्ति वस्तु तथोच्यते॥
units.translation: As an elephant conjured up by a magician is taken to be real because it is perceived to exist and also because it answers to the behaviour of a real elephant, so also external objects are taken to be real because they are perceived to exist and because one can deal with them.

units.label: Verse 4.45
units.deva:
जात्याभासं चलाभासं वस्त्वाभासं तथैव च।
अजाचलमवस्तुत्वं विज्ञानं शान्तमद्वयम्॥
units.translation: It is Consciousness, Vijñāna, alone that appears to be born or to move or to take the form of matter. But this Consciousness is really ever unborn, immovable and free from the traits of materiality; it is all peace and non-dual.

units.label: Verse 4.46
units.deva:
एवं न जायते चित्तमेवं धर्मा अजाः स्मृताः।
एवमेव विजानन्तो न पतन्ति विपर्यये॥
units.translation: Thus the mind is never subject to birth. All beings, too, are free from birth. Those who know this do not fall into false knowledge.

units.label: Verse 4.47
units.deva:
ऋजुवक्रादिकाभासमलातस्पन्दितं यथा।
ग्रहणग्राहकाभासं विज्ञानस्पन्दितं तथा॥
units.translation: As the line made by a moving fire-brand (Alāta, red-hot tipped poker) appears to be straight, crooked, etc., so Consciousness, when set in motion, appears as the perceiver, the perceived and the like.

units.label: Verse 4.48
units.deva:
अस्पन्दमानमलातमनाभासमजं यथा।
अस्पन्दमानं विज्ञानमनाभासमजं तथा॥
units.translation: As the fire-brand, when not in motion, is free from all appearances and remains changeless, so Consciousness, when not in motion, is free from all appearances and remains Changeless.

units.label: Verse 4.49
units.deva:
अलाते स्पन्दमाने वै नाभासा अन्यतोभुवः।
न ततोऽन्यत्र निःस्पन्दान्नालातं प्रविशन्ति ते॥
units.translation: When the fire-brand is set in motion, the appearances that are seen in it do not come from elsewhere. When it is still, the appearances do not leave the motionless fire-brand and go elsewhere, nor do they enter into the fire-brand itself.

units.label: Verse 4.50
units.deva:
न निर्गता अलातात्ते द्रव्यत्वाभावयोगतः।
विज्ञानेऽपि तथैव स्युराभासस्याविशेषतः॥
units.translation: The appearances do not emerge from the fire-brand, because their nature is not that of a substance. This applies likewise to Consciousness, because of the similarity of the appearances.

units.label: Verses 4.51–4.52
units.deva:
विज्ञाने स्पन्दमाने वै नाभासा अन्यतोभुवः।
न ततोऽन्यत्र निःस्पन्दान्न विज्ञानं विशन्ति ते॥
न निर्गतास्ते विज्ञानाद्द्रव्यत्वाभावयोगतः।
कार्यकारणताभावाद्यतोऽचिन्त्याः सदैव ते॥
units.translation: 51. When Consciousness is associated with the idea of activity, as in the waking and dream states, the appearances that seem to arise do not come from anywhere else. When Consciousness is non-active, as in deep sleep, the appearances do not leave the non-active Consciousness and go elsewhere, nor do they merge in it. 52. The appearances do not emerge from Consciousness, for their nature is not that of a substance. They are incomprehensible, because they are not subject to the relation of cause and effect.

units.label: Verse 4.53
units.deva:
द्रव्यं द्रव्यस्य हेतुः स्यादन्यदन्यस्य चैव हि।
द्रव्यत्वमन्यभावो वा धर्माणां नोपपद्यते॥
units.translation: A substance may be the cause of another substance and a non-substance, the cause of another non-substance. But the jīvas cannot possibly be anything like a substance or a non-substance.

units.label: Verse 4.54
units.deva:
एवं न चित्तजा धर्माश्चित्तं वापि न धर्मजम्।
एवं हेतुफलाजातिं प्रविशन्ति मनीषिणः॥
units.translation: Thus external appearances (objects) are not caused by the mind, nor is the mind caused by them. Hence thoughtful people hold to the principle of absolute non-creation.

units.label: Verse 4.55
units.deva:
यावद्धेतुफलावेशस्तावद्धेतुफलोद्भवः।
क्षीणे हेतुफलावेशे नास्ति हेतुफलोद्भवः॥
units.translation: As long as a person clings to the belief in causality, he will find cause producing effect. But when this attachment to causality wears away, cause and effect become non-existent.

units.label: Verse 4.56
units.deva:
यावद्धेतुफलावेशः संसारस्तावदायतः।
क्षीणे हेतुफलावेशे संसारं न प्रपद्यते॥
units.translation: As long as a person clings to the belief in causality, saṃsāra will continue to expand for him. But when this attachment to causality wears away, saṃsāra becomes non-existent.

units.label: Verse 4.57
units.deva:
संवृत्या जायते सर्वं शाश्वतं नास्ति तेन वै।
सद्भावेन ह्यजं सर्वमुच्छेदस्तेन नास्ति वै॥
units.translation: The entire universe is created by false knowledge; therefore nothing in it is eternal. Everything, again, as one with Ultimate Reality, is unborn; therefore there is no such thing as destruction.

units.label: Verse 4.58
units.deva:
धर्मा य इति जायन्ते जायन्ते ते न तत्त्वतः।
जन्म मायोपमं तेषां सा च माया न विद्यते॥
units.translation: Birth is ascribed to the jīvas; but such birth is not possible from the standpoint of Reality. Their birth is like that of an illusory object. That illusion, again, does not exist.

units.label: Verse 4.59
units.deva:
यथा मायामयाद्बीजाज्जायते तन्मयोऽङ्कुरः।
नासौ नित्यो न चोच्छेदी तद्वद्धर्मेषु योजना॥
units.translation: The illusory sprout is born of the illusory seed. This illusory sprout is neither permanent nor destructible. The same applies to the jīvas.

units.label: Verse 4.60
units.deva:
नाजेषु सर्वधर्मेषु शाश्वताशाश्वताभिधा।
यत्र वर्णा न वर्तन्ते विवेकस्तत्र नोच्यते॥
units.translation: The term permanent or impermanent cannot be applied to the birthless jīvas. What is indescribable in words cannot be discriminated about as permanent or impermanent.

units.label: Verses 4.61–4.62
units.deva:
यथा स्वप्ने द्वयाभासं चित्तं चलति मायया।
तथा जाग्रद्द्वयाभासं चित्तं चलति मायया॥
अद्वयं च द्वयाभासं चित्तं स्वप्ने न संशयः।
अद्वयं च द्वयाभासं तथा जाग्रन्न संशयः॥
units.translation: As in dreams the mind acts through māyā, presenting the appearance of duality, so also in the waking state the mind acts through māyā, presenting the appearance of duality. There is no doubt that the mind, which is in reality non-dual, appears to be dual in dreams; likewise, there is no doubt that what is non-dual i.e. Ātman, appears to be dual in the waking state.

units.label: Verse 4.63
units.deva:
स्वप्नदृक्प्रचरन्स्वप्ने दिक्षु वै दशसु स्थितान्।
अण्डजान्स्वेदजान्वापि जीवान्पश्यति यान्सदा॥
units.translation: The dreamer, wandering about in all the ten directions in his dream, sees the whole variety of jīvas, born of eggs, moisture, etc.

units.label: Verse 4.64
units.deva:
स्वप्नदृक्चित्तदृश्यास्ते न विद्यन्ते ततः पृथक्।
तथा तद्दृश्यमेवेदं स्वप्नदृक्चित्तमिष्यते॥
units.translation: These entities, which are objects of the mind of the dreamer, do not exist apart from his mind. Likewise, the mind of the dreamer is an object of perception of the dreamer alone.

units.label: Verses 4.65–4.66
units.deva:
चरञ्जागरिते जाग्रद्दिक्षु वै दशसु स्थितान्।
अण्डजान्स्वेदजान्वापि जीवान्पश्यति यान्सदा॥
जाग्रच्चित्तेक्षणीयास्ते न विद्यन्ते ततः पृथक्।
तथा तद्दृश्यमेवेदं जाग्रतश्चित्तमिष्यते॥
units.translation: 65. The waking man, wandering about in all the ten directions in his waking state, sees the whole variety of jīvas, born of eggs, moisture, etc. 66. They are the objects of the mind of the waking man and do not exist apart from it. Likewise, the mind of the waking man is an object of his perception alone.

units.label: Verse 4.67
units.deva:
उभे ह्यन्योन्यदृश्ये ते किं तदस्तीति चोच्यते।
लक्षणाशून्यमुभयं तन्मतेनैव गृह्यते॥
units.translation: Both the mind and the jīvas are objects of each other’s perception. Can the one exist independent of the other? The reply of the wise is in the negative. There is no evidence of the existence of the one without the other; they are cognized only through each other.

units.label: Verses 4.68–4.70
units.deva:
यथा स्वप्नमयो जीवो जायते म्रियतेऽपि च।
तथा जीवा अमी सर्वे भवन्ति न भवन्ति च॥
यथा मायामयो जीवो जायते म्रियतेऽपि च।
तथा जीवा अमी सर्वे भवन्ति न भवन्ति च॥
यथा निर्मितको जीवो जायते म्रियतेऽपि च।
तथा जीवा अमी सर्वे भवन्ति न भवन्ति च॥
units.translation: 68. As the dream jīva comes into existence and disappears, so also these jīvas perceived in the waking state appear and disappear. 69. As the jīva conjured up by the magician comes into existence and disappears, so also these jīvas perceived in the waking state appear and disappear. 70. As an artificial jīva comes into existence and disappears, so also these jīvas perceived in the waking state appear and disappear.

units.label: Verse 4.71
units.deva:
न कश्चिज्जायते जीवः सम्भवोऽस्य न विद्यते।
एतत्तदुत्तमं सत्यं यत्र किञ्चिन्न जायते॥
units.translation: No jīva ever comes into existence. There exists no cause that can produce it. The supreme truth is that nothing ever is born.

units.label: Verse 4.72
units.deva:
चित्तस्पन्दितमेवेदं ग्राह्यग्राहकवद्द्वयम्।
चित्तं निर्विषयं नित्यमसङ्गं तेन कीर्तितम्॥
units.translation: The world of duality, which is perceived to exist and is characterized by the subject-object relationship, is verily a movement of the mind. The mind, again, from the standpoint of Reality has no contact with any object. Hence it is declared to be eternal and unattached.

units.label: Verse 4.73
units.deva:
योऽस्ति कल्पितसंवृत्या परमार्थेन नास्त्यसौ।
परतन्त्राभिसंवृत्या स्यान्नास्ति परमार्थतः॥
units.translation: That which exists on the strength of false knowledge based upon imagination does not really exist. Again, that which is said to exist on the strength of the views advanced by other schools of thought does not really exist.

units.label: Verse 4.74
units.deva:
अजः कल्पितसंवृत्या परमार्थेन नाप्यजः।
परतन्त्राभिनिष्पत्त्या संवृत्या जायते तु सः॥
units.translation: Ātman is called birthless (a-ja) from the standpoint of false knowledge based upon imagination; in reality It is not even birthless. The unborn Ātman is said to be born from the standpoint of the false knowledge cherished by other schools of thought.

units.label: Verse 4.75
units.deva:
अभूताभिनिवेशोऽस्ति द्वयं तत्र न विद्यते।
द्वयाभावं स बुद्ध्वैव निर्निमित्तो न जायते॥
units.translation: People persistently hold to the idea of unreality i.e. duality. But such duality does not exist. One who has realized the absence of duality is not born again, since there remains no longer any cause for his birth.

units.label: Verse 4.76
units.deva:
यदा न लभते हेतूनुत्तमाधममध्यमान्।
तदा न जायते चित्तं हेत्वभावे फलं कुतः॥
units.translation: When the mind finds no cause – superior, inferior, or middling – it becomes free from birth. How can there be an effect without a cause?

units.label: Verse 4.77
units.deva:
अनिमित्तस्य चित्तस्य यानुत्पत्तिः समाद्वया।
अजातस्यैव सर्वस्य चित्तदृश्यं हि तद्यतः॥
units.translation: The birthlessness of the mind, which is free from manifestation and causal relationship, is absolute and constant. For duality i.e. the perceiving mind and its objects is merely an objectification of the mind.

units.label: Verse 4.78
units.deva:
बुद्ध्वानिमित्ततां सत्यां हेतुं पृथगनाप्नुवन्।
वीतशोकं तथा काममभयं पदमश्नुते॥
units.translation: Realizing the absence of causality as ultimate truth and not finding any other reason for birth, one attains that state which is free from grief, desire and fear.

units.label: Verse 4.79
units.deva:
अभूताभिनिवेशाद्धि सदृशे तत्प्रवर्तते।
वस्त्वभावं स बुद्ध्वैव निःसङ्गं विनिवर्तते॥
units.translation: On account of attachment to unreal objects the mind pursues such objects. But it comes back to its pure state when it attains non-attachment, realizing their unreality.

units.label: Verse 4.80
units.deva:
निवृत्तस्याप्रवृत्तस्य निश्चला हि तदा स्थितिः।
विषयः स हि बुद्धानां तत्साम्यमजमद्वयम्॥
units.translation: The mind freed from attachment to all external objects and undistracted by fresh objects attains the state of immutability. The wise realize such a mind to be Brahman; It is undifferentiated, birthless and non-dual.

units.label: Verse 4.81
units.deva:
अजमनिद्रमस्वप्नं प्रभातं भवति स्वयम्।
सकृद्विभातो ह्येवैष धर्मो धातुस्वभावतः॥
units.translation: The birthless, dreamless and sleepless Reality reveals Itself by Itself; for this Dharma (Ātman) by Its very nature is self-luminous.

units.label: Verse 4.82
units.deva:
सुखम् आव्रियते नित्यं दुःखं विव्रियते सदा।
यस्य कस्य च धर्मस्य ग्रहेण भगवानसौ॥
units.translation: The Lord (Ātman) becomes easily hidden because of attachment to any single object and is revealed with great difficulty.

units.label: Verse 4.83
units.deva:
अस्ति नास्त्यस्ति नास्तीति नास्ति नास्तीति वा पुनः।
चलस्थिरोभयाभावैरावृणोत्येव बालिशः॥
units.translation: The ignorant, with their childish minds, verily cover Ātman by predicating of It such attributes as existence, non-existence, existence and non-existence and total non-existence, deriving these characteristics from the notions of change, immovability, combination of change and immovability and absolute negation which they associate with Ātman.

units.label: Verse 4.84
units.deva:
कोट्यश्चतस्र एतास्तु ग्रहैर्यासां सदावृतः।
भगवानाभिरस्पृष्टो येन दृष्टः स सर्वदृक्॥
units.translation: These are the four theories regarding Ātman, through attachment to which It always remains hidden from one’s view. He who knows the Lord to he ever untouched by them indeed knows all.

units.label: Verse 4.85
units.deva:
प्राप्य सर्वज्ञतां कृत्स्नां ब्राह्मण्यं पदमद्वयम्।
अनापन्नादिमध्यान्तं किमतः परमीहते॥
units.translation: What else remains to be desired by him who has attained the state of the brahmin – a state of complete omniscience and non-duality, which is without beginning, middle, or end?

units.label: Verse 4.86
units.deva:
विप्राणां विनयो ह्येष शमः प्राकृत उच्यते।
दमः प्रकृतिदान्तत्वादेवं विद्वाञ्शमं व्रजेत्॥
units.translation: The humility (vinaya) of the brāhmaṇas is natural. Their tranquillity (śama) is also natural. Further, the control of the senses (dama) comes natural to them. He who has realized Brahman attains peace.

units.label: Verse 4.87
units.deva:
सवस्तु सोपलम्भं च द्वयं लौकिकमिष्यते।
अवस्तु सोपलम्भं च शुद्धं लौकिकमिष्यते॥
units.translation: Vedānta recognizes the ordinary state of waking, in which duality, consisting of objects and the idea of coming in contact with them, is admitted. It also recognizes a purer ordinary state i.e. the dream state, in which is experienced duality consisting of objects and the idea of coming in contact with them, though such objects do not exist.

units.label: Verse 4.88
units.deva:
अवस्त्वनुपलम्भं च लोकोत्तरमिति स्मृतम्।
ज्ञानं ज्ञेयं च विज्ञेयं सदा बुद्धैः प्रकीर्तितम्॥
units.translation: The wise recognize another state, in which there exist neither objects nor ideas regarding them. This state is beyond all empirical experiences. They describe the three: knowledge, the objects of knowledge i.e. the three states and the supremely knowable i.e. Ultimate Reality.

units.label: Verse 4.89
units.deva:
ज्ञाने च त्रिविधे ज्ञेये क्रमेण विदिते स्वयम्।
सर्वज्ञता हि सर्वत्र भवतीह महाधियः॥
units.translation: Having known knowledge and the threefold knowable, one after another, the knower, endowed with supreme intellect, attains in this very life and everywhere, the state of omniscience.

units.label: Verse 4.90
units.deva:
हेयज्ञेयाप्यपाक्यानि विज्ञेयान्यग्रयाणतः।
तेषामन्यत्र विज्ञेयादुपलम्भस्त्रिषु स्मृतः॥
units.translation: One should be conversant, at the very outset, with four things. These are as follows: the things to be avoided, the goal to be realized, the disciplines to be cultivated and the tendencies to be rendered ineffective. Of these four, all except the goal to be realized i.e. the Supreme Reality exist only as products of the imagination.

units.label: Verse 4.91
units.deva:
प्रकृत्याकाशवज्ज्ञेयाः सर्वे धर्मा अनादयः।
विद्यते न हि नानात्वं तेषां क्वचन किञ्चन॥
units.translation: All Ātmans (Dharmas) are to be known, by their very nature, to be beginningless and unattached like ākāśa. There is not the slightest variety in there in any way or at any time.

units.label: Verse 4.92
units.deva:
आदिबुद्धाः प्रकृत्यैव सर्वे धर्माः सुनिश्चिताः।
यस्यैवं भवति क्षान्तिः सोऽमृतत्वाय कल्पते॥
units.translation: All jīvas are, by their very nature, illumined from the very beginning. There can never be any doubt about their nature. He who, having known this, rests without seeking further knowledge is alone capable of attaining Immortality.

units.label: Verse 4.93
units.deva:
आदिशान्ता ह्यनुत्पन्नाः प्रकृत्यैव सुनिर्वृताः।
सर्वे धर्माः समाभिन्ना अजं साम्यं विशारदम्॥
units.translation: The jīvas, from the very beginning and by their very nature, are all peace, unborn and completely free. They are characterized by sameness and non-separateness. The unborn Ātman is always established in sameness and purity.

units.label: Verse 4.94
units.deva:
वैशारद्यं तु वै नास्ति भेदे विचरतां सदा।
भेदनिम्नाः पृथग्वादास्तस्मात्ते कृपणाः स्मृताः॥
units.translation: Those who always wander in the realm of separateness cannot realize the purity of Ātman. Their minds are inclined to differentiation and they assert the separateness of the Ātmans. Therefore they are called narrow-minded.

units.label: Verse 4.95
units.deva:
अजे साम्ये तु ये केचिद्भविष्यन्ति सुनिश्चिताः।
ते हि लोके महाज्ञानास्तच्च लोको न गाहते॥
units.translation: They alone in this world are endowed with the highest wisdom who are firm in their conviction of the sameness and birthlessness of Ātman. The ordinary man does not understand their way.

units.label: Verse 4.96
units.deva:
अजेष्वजमसंक्रान्तं धर्मेषु ज्ञानमिष्यते।
यतो न क्रमते ज्ञानमसङ्गं तेन कीर्तितम्॥
units.translation: Knowledge, which is the very essence of the unborn jīvas, is itself called unborn and unrelated. This Knowledge is proclaimed to be unattached, since it is unrelated to any other object.

units.label: Verse 4.97
units.deva:
अणुमात्रेऽपि वैधर्म्ये जायमानेऽविपश्चितः।
असङ्गता सदा नास्ति किमुतावरणच्युतिः॥
units.translation: To those ignorant people who believe that Ātman can deviate from Its true nature even in the slightest measure, Its eternally unrelated character is lost. In that case the destruction of the veil is out of the question.

units.label: Verse 4.98
units.deva:
अलब्धावरणाः सर्वे धर्माः प्रकृतिनिर्मलाः।
आदौ बुद्धास्तथा मुक्ता बुध्यन्त इति नायकाः॥
units.translation: All jīvas are ever free from bondage and pure by nature. They are illumined and free from the very beginning. Yet the wise speak of the jīvas as capable of knowing Ultimate Reality.

units.label: Verse 4.99
units.deva:
क्रमते न हि बुद्धस्य ज्ञानं धर्मेषु तायिनः।
सर्वे धर्मास्तथा ज्ञानं नैतद्बुद्धेन भाषितम्॥
units.translation: The Knowledge of the wise man, who is all light, is never related to any object. All the jīvas, as well as Knowledge, are ever unrelated to objects. This is not the view of Buddha.

units.label: Verse 4.100
units.deva:
दुर्दर्शमतिगम्भीरमजं साम्यं विशारदम्।
बुद्ध्वा पदमनानात्वं नमस्कुर्मो यथाबलम्॥
units.translation: Having realized the Knowledge of the Supreme Reality, which is hard to grasp, profound, birthless, the same throughout, all light and free from multiplicity, we salute It as best we can.
